AK.acceptedOptions: Official voter registration card; birth certificate; hunting or fishing license; current utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, government check, or other government document showing the voter's name and address.
AK.alternativeIfNoDocument: Election official may waive the ID requirement if the official knows the voter; otherwise the voter may cast a questioned ballot.
AK.keyCaveat: Ordinary in-person voters can satisfy the rule with several non-photo documents.

AL.alternativeIfNoDocument: Two election officials may identify the voter and sign sworn statements, or the voter can cast a provisional ballot and later show photo ID.
AL.keyCaveat: NCSL notes Alabama is sometimes described as effectively strict because provisional voters generally must later show photo ID.

AR.alternativeIfNoDocument: Provisional ballot; counted only if acceptable ID is shown by noon on the Monday after the election.
AR.keyCaveat: Arkansas requires photo identification for ordinary in-person voting.

AS.acceptedOptions: If the voter lacks a valid American Samoa voter ID card with photo or a valid U.S. passport, the voter may use a combination of two IDs: another government-issued photo ID plus a birth certificate.
AS.alternativeIfNoDocument: The reviewed source did not identify a broader standalone non-photo alternative beyond the paired-ID option.
AS.keyCaveat: The non-photo document (birth certificate) is accepted only as part of a two-ID combination under the source reviewed.

AZ.acceptedOptions: Utility bill dated within 90 days; bank or credit-union statement dated within 90 days; Arizona vehicle registration; Indian census card; property tax statement; vehicle insurance card; recorder's certificate.
AZ.alternativeIfNoDocument: Provisional ballot; counted only if ID is provided to the county recorder within the cure period.
AZ.keyCaveat: These documentary options can be used instead of photo ID for ordinary in-person voting.

CA.acceptedOptions: No ID document is ordinarily required at the polls.
CA.alternativeIfNoDocument: Voter states name and address and signs the poll book.
CA.keyCaveat: This reflects ordinary in-person voting, not special first-time-by-mail HAVA cases.

CO.acceptedOptions: Current utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck, or other government document showing name and address; Medicare or Medicaid card; certified birth certificate; certified documentation of naturalization.
CO.alternativeIfNoDocument: Provisional ballot; election officials verify eligibility before counting.
CO.keyCaveat: Most Colorado voters vote by mail, but this list applies to in-person voters at vote centers/polling places.

CT.acceptedOptions: Social Security card; any other preprinted form of identification showing the elector's name and either address, signature, or photo.
CT.alternativeIfNoDocument: Voter can complete a signed statement with residential address and date of birth under penalty of false statement.
CT.keyCaveat: Connecticut accepts several non-photo documents for ordinary in-person voting.

DC.acceptedOptions: No ID document is ordinarily required at the polls.
DC.keyCaveat: The District uses signature-based verification for ordinary in-person voting.

DE.acceptedOptions: Utility bill; paycheck; government document showing the voter's name and address.
DE.alternativeIfNoDocument: Voter may sign an affidavit of affirmation.
DE.keyCaveat: Non-photo documents are sufficient if they show the required information.

FL.acceptedOptions: No standalone non-photo document list for ordinary in-person voting.
FL.alternativeIfNoDocument: If the picture ID lacks the voter's signature, an additional ID showing the signature is required; otherwise the voter may cast a provisional ballot and the signature on the envelope is checked.
FL.keyCaveat: A non-photo item can supplement a picture ID for signature purposes, but not replace the ordinary picture-ID requirement.

GA.alternativeIfNoDocument: Provisional ballot; counted only if photo ID is shown within the cure period.
GA.keyCaveat: Georgia requires photo ID for ordinary in-person voting.

GU.acceptedOptions: The U.S. Vote Foundation source reviewed did not identify a standalone non-photo document option for ordinary in-person voting. It listed passport, current/valid photo ID, tribal ID, student ID, military ID, ID issued by another state, government photo ID, and Guam driver's license.
GU.alternativeIfNoDocument: No broader non-photo document substitute was clearly identified in the source reviewed.
GU.keyCaveat: Because the reviewed territory source emphasized photo-style IDs, this row is flagged for caution rather than stated as a definitive 'No'.

HI.acceptedOptions: No ID document is ordinarily required at the polls.
HI.alternativeIfNoDocument: Voter provides name, address, and date of birth.
HI.keyCaveat: This is the ordinary in-person rule after Hawaii repealed its prior request-for-ID provision.

IA.acceptedOptions: Current signed voter identification card; residential lease; property tax statement; utility bill; bank statement; paycheck; government check; other government document; or a written oath by another registered voter in the precinct.
IA.alternativeIfNoDocument: Provisional ballot if the voter cannot use any listed document or attesting-voter option.
IA.keyCaveat: Iowa accepts several documentary proofs of identity/residency for ordinary in-person voting.

ID.alternativeIfNoDocument: Voter may complete an affidavit with name and address in lieu of presenting ID.
ID.keyCaveat: Idaho's alternative is affidavit-based, not document-based.

IL.acceptedOptions: No ID document is ordinarily required at the polls.
IL.alternativeIfNoDocument: Voter signs an affidavit of eligibility and gives name and, if requested, address.
IL.keyCaveat: Ordinary in-person voters do not generally need to present a document.

IN.alternativeIfNoDocument: Voter casts a provisional ballot; it can count if the voter later shows photo ID or executes an indigency or religious-objection affidavit.
IN.keyCaveat: Educational-institution IDs may not be used for voting effective July 1, 2025.

KS.alternativeIfNoDocument: Provisional ballot; voter must later provide valid photo ID before the canvass.
KS.keyCaveat: Kansas requires photo identification for ordinary in-person voting.

KY.acceptedOptions: After signing a voter affirmation form and stating the reason for lacking photo ID, a voter may use a Social Security card, county-issued identification card, food-stamp identification card, or another identification card with photo and name.
KY.alternativeIfNoDocument: Limited document exception exists only after the voter affirmation step.
KY.keyCaveat: The listed exception includes both non-photo and photo documents; it is not a standalone non-photo system.

LA.acceptedOptions: If the voter has no picture ID, the voter may sign an affidavit and provide a current registration certificate, date of birth, or other precinct-register information requested by commissioners.
LA.alternativeIfNoDocument: Affidavit path is available, but the voter can still be challenged.
LA.keyCaveat: Louisiana's documentary alternative is tied to an affidavit and poll-book information.

MA.acceptedOptions: No ID document is ordinarily required at the polls.
MA.alternativeIfNoDocument: Voter provides name and, if requested, address.
MA.keyCaveat: Massachusetts ordinarily verifies identity without a document at the polls.

MD.acceptedOptions: No ID document is ordinarily required at the polls.
MD.alternativeIfNoDocument: Voter states month and date of birth and, in some circumstances, address.
MD.keyCaveat: Ordinary in-person voters do not generally present a document.

ME.acceptedOptions: No ID document is ordinarily required at the polls.
ME.keyCaveat: Maine uses non-documentary verification for ordinary in-person voting.

MI.alternativeIfNoDocument: A voter who does not possess or did not bring photo ID may sign an affidavit and vote a regular ballot.
MI.keyCaveat: Michigan's ordinary listed IDs are photo IDs; the fallback is affidavit-based.

MN.acceptedOptions: No ID document is ordinarily required at the polls.
MN.alternativeIfNoDocument: Voter signs an affidavit of eligibility and, if requested, provides name, address, and date of birth.
MN.keyCaveat: Ordinary in-person voters do not generally need to present a document.

MO.alternativeIfNoDocument: Provisional ballot; it can count if the voter returns by 7 p.m. on Election Day with ID or if the provisional-ballot-envelope signature matches the registration record.
MO.keyCaveat: Missouri's alternative is signature or same-day cure, not a non-photo document list.

MP.acceptedOptions: No ordinary non-photo document list identified in the reviewed source.
MP.alternativeIfNoDocument: The reviewed source states that a current and valid photo ID is required for in-person voting.
MP.keyCaveat: The U.S. Vote Foundation page reviewed lists only a current and valid photo ID for in-person voting.

MS.alternativeIfNoDocument: Affidavit ballot; generally counted only if the voter later shows government-issued photo ID or returns with a religious-objection affidavit.
MS.keyCaveat: Mississippi is a photo-ID state with narrow affidavit-ballot exceptions.

MT.acceptedOptions: Two alternative IDs are allowed if one has a photo; documentary options include current utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, notice of confirmation of voter registration, government check, or other government document showing the elector's name and current address.
MT.alternativeIfNoDocument: Provisional ballot; eligibility is later checked by signature verification.
MT.keyCaveat: Montana does accept documents, but one of the two alternative IDs must include a photo.

NC.acceptedOptions: No ordinary non-photo document option identified in the NCSL in-effect table.
NC.alternativeIfNoDocument: Limited statutory exception paths apply for certain voters; otherwise the voter uses the photo-ID cure/exception process.
NC.keyCaveat: North Carolina is currently listed by NCSL as a strict photo-ID state.

ND.acceptedOptions: If the primary ID is missing required or current information, it may be supplemented with a current utility bill, current bank statement, government-issued check, paycheck, federal/state/local government document, or authorized university document; certain voters may use a long-term-care certificate.
ND.alternativeIfNoDocument: Set-aside ballot/provisional-style process if the voter later shows valid ID within the cure period.
ND.keyCaveat: North Dakota requires the voter record to show legal name, current residential street address, and date of birth.

NE.acceptedOptions: A record from a hospital, assisted-living facility, provider agency for disability services, or intermediate-care facility.
NE.alternativeIfNoDocument: Voter fills out a provisional voter-identification-verification envelope.
NE.keyCaveat: Nebraska's photo-ID law still lists this facility record as an acceptable form of ID.

NH.alternativeIfNoDocument: A moderator, supervisor of the checklist, or clerk may verify the voter's identity; otherwise the voter is not allowed to vote under the current law.
NH.keyCaveat: New Hampshire removed earlier no-photo provisional-ballot processes in 2024.

NJ.acceptedOptions: No ID document is ordinarily required at the polls.
NJ.alternativeIfNoDocument: Voter provides a signature that is compared with the signature on file.

NM.acceptedOptions: No ID document is ordinarily required at the polls.
NM.alternativeIfNoDocument: Voter provides written or verbal confirmation of name, address, and date of birth, then signs the poll book.
NM.keyCaveat: Ordinary in-person voters are verified without showing a document.

NV.acceptedOptions: No ID document is ordinarily required at the polls.
NV.alternativeIfNoDocument: Voter signs the poll book; signature is compared to the signature on file.
NV.keyCaveat: Nevada generally verifies ordinary in-person voters by signature.

NY.acceptedOptions: No ID document is ordinarily required at the polls.
NY.alternativeIfNoDocument: Voter signs the poll book; officials compare the signature and may compare physical appearance with the record.
NY.keyCaveat: Ordinary in-person voting is generally signature-based.

OH.alternativeIfNoDocument: Provisional ballot; voters with a religious objection to being photographed can complete an affidavit.
OH.keyCaveat: Ohio became a photo-ID state under 2023 legislation.

OK.acceptedOptions: County voter registration card may serve as proof of identity without meeting the usual photo-ID criteria.
OK.alternativeIfNoDocument: Provisional ballot can count if affidavit data matches the registration database.
OK.keyCaveat: NCSL notes some observers still describe Oklahoma as a photo-ID state because most voters use photo ID.

OR.acceptedOptions: No ID document is ordinarily required; Oregon mainly votes by mail.
OR.alternativeIfNoDocument: Voter signs the return envelope, including when voting in person at a county election office.
OR.keyCaveat: Ordinary verification is signature-based rather than document-based.

PA.acceptedOptions: No ID document is ordinarily required at the polls.
PA.alternativeIfNoDocument: Voter signs an affidavit of eligibility and provides address except in certain circumstances.
PA.keyCaveat: Ordinary in-person voters generally do not show a document.

PR.acceptedOptions: No ordinary non-photo document list identified in the reviewed source.
PR.alternativeIfNoDocument: The reviewed source lists U.S. passport, U.S. Global Entry card, valid military ID, valid Puerto Rico driver's license, and valid Puerto Rico voter ID card.
PR.keyCaveat: Puerto Rico's reviewed source was photo-ID-based for in-person voting.

RI.alternativeIfNoDocument: Provisional ballot; local board later checks whether the signature matches the registration record.
RI.keyCaveat: Rhode Island's accepted IDs must show a photo.

SC.acceptedOptions: If the voter has a reasonable impediment to obtaining photo ID, the voter may show a current non-photo voter registration card and sign an affidavit.
SC.alternativeIfNoDocument: Without the reasonable-impediment path, the voter can cast a provisional ballot and later show photo ID.
SC.keyCaveat: The non-photo registration card works only inside the reasonable-impediment exception.

SD.alternativeIfNoDocument: Voter may complete an affidavit in lieu of personal identification.
SD.keyCaveat: South Dakota's fallback is affidavit-based rather than document-based.

TN.alternativeIfNoDocument: Most voters use a provisional ballot and later show photo ID; indigent voters and voters with a religious objection to being photographed can execute an affidavit of identity.
TN.keyCaveat: Tennessee is a strict photo-ID state for ordinary in-person voting.

TX.acceptedOptions: With a Reasonable Impediment Declaration: valid voter registration certificate; certified birth certificate; current utility bill; bank statement; government check; paycheck; or government document with the voter's name and address.
TX.alternativeIfNoDocument: Reasonable Impediment Declaration is required with the supporting document; some voters also qualify for disability, religious-objection, or natural-disaster paths.
TX.keyCaveat: Texas accepts these documents only through the reasonable-impediment system, not as a standalone universal substitute.

UT.acceptedOptions: Two forms of ID that bear the voter's name and provide evidence that the voter resides in the precinct.
UT.alternativeIfNoDocument: Provisional ballot; county clerk may also verify identity and residence through other means.
UT.keyCaveat: Utah allows documentary proof of residence instead of a single photo ID.

VA.acceptedOptions: Voter confirmation document; copy of a current utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck, or other government document containing the voter's name and address.
VA.alternativeIfNoDocument: Except for certain HAVA first-time voters, a voter without ID can sign a statement verifying identity and vote a regular ballot.
VA.keyCaveat: Virginia keeps both documentary and signed-statement paths for ordinary in-person voting.

VI.acceptedOptions: If a voter is voting for the first time or the registration is incomplete, the reviewed source says valid ID may be required; accepted documents include valid U.S. passport, certified/copy of U.S. birth certificate, military discharge certificate, birth certificate, or certified/copy of a naturalization document.
VI.alternativeIfNoDocument: For established voters, the reviewed source suggests ID is not generally required unless the first-time/incomplete-registration condition applies.
VI.keyCaveat: This is a conditional rule from the reviewed source, not a universal always-on document requirement for every in-person voter.

VT.acceptedOptions: No ID document is ordinarily required at the polls.
VT.alternativeIfNoDocument: Voter states name and, if requested, address; NCSL also notes documentation may be provided if requested.
VT.keyCaveat: The NCSL no-document summary does not specify the exact documentation types for Vermont's alternative path.

WA.acceptedOptions: No standalone non-photo document list. At a voting center, a voter may ordinarily sign a ballot declaration instead of presenting ID; if identification is used, it must be photo ID.
WA.alternativeIfNoDocument: Provisional ballot can count if the signature on the declaration matches the registration record.
WA.keyCaveat: Most Washington voters vote by mail; this row addresses in-person vote-center voting.

WI.acceptedOptions: No ordinary non-photo document list for voter ID itself.
WI.alternativeIfNoDocument: Provisional ballot; voter must later furnish statutory photo ID. Separate proof-of-residence rules can also apply when the photo ID does not prove residence.
WI.keyCaveat: Wisconsin voters approved a 2025 constitutional amendment requiring photo ID to vote.

WV.acceptedOptions: No ordinary non-photo document list in the current law.
WV.alternativeIfNoDocument: An adult who has known the voter for at least six months may sign an affidavit, or a poll worker who has known the voter for at least six months may allow voting; otherwise the voter may cast a provisional ballot after an identity affidavit.
WV.keyCaveat: NCSL notes West Virginia enacted a 2025 law changing the state from a non-photo to a photo-ID system.

WY.acceptedOptions: Valid Medicare insurance card or valid Medicaid insurance card (accepted until Dec. 31, 2029).
WY.alternativeIfNoDocument: Provisional ballot; voter must furnish statutory ID by the close of business on the day after the election.
WY.keyCaveat: Most Wyoming voters still use photo ID, but these non-photo insurance cards are currently valid.
